intent: The button that backs out of an alert dialog without confirming, closing it.
typical_uses: The answer that leaves things as they were, such as Cancel or Keep editing

dont_use_when.situation: The answer that confirms the question

invariants.text: AlertDialogCancel is the primitive's Close rendered as the kit's Button: a press runs the caller's `onClick` and closes the alert dialog.

anti_patterns.dont: Look for `loading` or `icon` on the cancel
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep the cancel a plain caption; it takes only Button's `variant` and `size`, and the busy state belongs to AlertDialogAction

a11y.by: the primitive's Dialog.Close rendered through the kit's Button; alert-dialog.test.tsx asserts the cancel is found by role button under its caption ("Cancel") and that pressing it removes the alertdialog

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies, including the kit Button the part renders by default
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. alert-dialog.tsx spreads the caller's props after its own `render`, so a caller's `render` drops the Button and with it `variant` and `size`.

style.states: style accepts a function of the button's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through `variant`/`size` and button.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A cancel with its own caption

bad.title: A made-up onCancel prop on the root
bad.why: No part takes `onCancel`; give the cancel its own `onClick`, or read the close through the root's `onOpenChange`.

cannot_extract: default: prop "render" is written before the rest spread as "{<Button variant={variant} size={size} />}", which is not a literal - the contract states no default for it
